title: Judge Says No: Trump Can't Get Georgia Election Workers' Private Info
summary: A federal judge just stopped former President Trump's team from getting the personal information of every election worker in Fulton County, Georgia. The judge said the request was unreasonable and too burdensome. Trump has claimed, without proof, that there was cheating in the 2020 election in that county. In other news, a tall building under construction in New York City almost collapsed! Beams were bent and floors were sagging. Firefighters rushed to the scene after bricks started falling. The building used to be the headquarters of Pfizer and is being turned into fancy apartments. No one was hurt, but people nearby had to leave their homes. And in Britain, politician Nigel Farage quit his job in Parliament because of questions about money he received. He says he'll run again right away, calling it a fight between the people and the establishment.
why_it_matters: These stories show that rules protect people's privacy, buildings must be safe, and leaders must answer to the public—all important lessons about fairness and safety.

background_read: Fulton County, Georgia (where Atlanta is) was a key place in the 2020 election dispute, and a federal judge said Trump's lawyers asked for too much personal data.
In big cities like New York, old buildings being turned into apartments must be carefully checked, because when beams bend, a collapse can happen.
In Britain, politician Nigel Farage (who led the campaign for the UK to leave the European Union) stepped down from Parliament after questions about his finances.
Article_Structure: WHO: A federal judge, Trump's team, a New York construction building, and politician Nigel Farage.
WHAT: The judge blocked the request for election workers' private info; a building almost collapsed; Farage resigned from law-making.
WHERE: Fulton County, Georgia; New York City; Britain.
WHY: The request was too burdensome; beams bent and floors sagged; there were questions about money Farage received.

perspectives.description: They were glad the judge stopped the request because election workers should not be harassed with demands for their personal information.
Some people believe Trump's team had a right to check the data to make sure elections are fair, and the judge blocked what they saw as a legitimate investigation.
Experts stress that old buildings need careful checks to prevent disasters, and developers should not rush to turn a profit if it puts people at risk.
